title: What Is a Hysterectomy?
description: What a hysterectomy is, what it is for and when it is indicated. Care in Lima with price alternatives.
tldr: Removal of the uterus because of fibroids, bleeding, prolapse or other conditions; it can be total or partial. The specialist decides the indication; results vary from person to person.
bodyHtml:
Removal of the uterus because of fibroids, bleeding, prolapse or other conditions; it can be total or partial.

How is it done?

Vaginal, laparoscopic or open depending on the case; the minimally invasive approach is preferred when possible.

When is it indicated?

Symptomatic fibroids, bleeding that cannot be controlled, prolapse or uterine disease. The gynecologist decides.

At Cirugía 24 Horas

We operate in Lima with the same team across different clinics, so you can choose the price alternative that fits you. We also care for patients from abroad.

faqs.q: Is a hysterectomy an outpatient procedure?
faqs.a: It depends on the procedure and the clinic; the specialist will tell you after the evaluation.

faqs.q: Who decides whether I need it?
faqs.a: The surgeon, after an evaluation with tests.

tldr: Usual candidates: symptomatic fibroids, bleeding that cannot be controlled, prolapse or uterine disease. The gynecologist decides. Final candidacy is decided by the surgeon after an evaluation with tests.
bodyHtml:
Am I a candidate for a hysterectomy?

Usual indications

Symptomatic fibroids, bleeding that cannot be controlled, prolapse or uterine disease. The gynecologist decides.

The evaluation

It includes a medical history and tests, and sometimes imaging. It does not depend solely on what the patient wants.

faqs.a: Medical or conservative treatments (depending on the cause) before surgery.

title: Risks and Complications of a Hysterectomy
description: Risks and possible complications of a hysterectomy and how they are reduced with evaluation and follow-up.
tldr: Like any surgery, a hysterectomy has risks: bleeding, infection, injury to nearby organs and thrombosis. They are uncommon and are reduced with proper evaluation, careful technique and follow-up. The surgeon explains them at the consultation.
bodyHtml:
Learning about the risks of a hysterectomy is part of a responsible decision.

Possible complications

Bleeding, infection, injury to nearby organs and thrombosis.

How they are reduced

A complete pre-operative evaluation, careful technique and close follow-up. The team's experience influences results.

faqs.a: It is a common procedure; safety depends on the evaluation, the technique and the follow-up.

faqs.q: What warning signs should I watch for?
faqs.a: Fever, heavy bleeding, severe pain or difficulty urinating.
